newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian gold reserves nearly empty -audit source.
newsitem.headline: Russian gold reserves nearly empty -audit source.

text.p: Russia's state stocks of gold are practically empty, according to a source in the Audit Chamber, referring to a chamber report completed September 1996.
"The report concluded that Russia's gold reserves in GosFond (the main reserve) are practically exhausted," said the source, who did not wish to be identified.

The report concerned the state of the defunct State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones, or Komdragmet, which was disbanded by presidential decree in mid-1996 and officially ceased functioning in November 1996.
Russian metals sources, including Lev Weinberg, a banker with close ties to the industry, have said that the state has not yet bought the bulk of gold produced by miners in 1996.
The reserves, known as GosFond, were once under the aegis of Komdragmet but have been renamed GosKhran and are now managed by the Finance Ministry.
